EXTEND C0004 | FIND — `scan_health()` only inserts keys into `tools_available` for tools it iterates, and on the `existing == []` early return it returns an empty dict. FOLLOW — consumers cannot distinguish “tool missing/unavailable” from “tool not reported at all”, and the report schema becomes shape-unstable across rounds/filesets. Any insect-brain logic or reviewer comparing availability over time will see missing keys instead of explicit `False`, which silently corrupts health telemetry. FIX — initialize `tools_available` with all expected tool names set to `False` before any early return/scan loop, then overwrite entries on successful availability detection.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not evaluate fixes in a real sandboxed project context. It copies only the target file to a tempdir (`patched_path = tmpdir/basename(target)`), then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that lone file. Whole-file fixes or edits that depend on sibling modules/imports are therefore analyzed outside the original package layout. Evidence: the implementation never copies package directories, config files, or imported local modules into `tmpdir`; post-fix checks are run only on `patched_path`.
FOLLOW: This can misclassify harmful fixes as SAFE/NEUTRAL or safe fixes as harmful. Relative imports, package-qualified imports, pyright config discovery, and lint/security context can all differ when the file is detached from its repo. Because immune stage 4 marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns SAFE/NEUTRAL, a false-safe verdict can close a bug in later NK dedup logic and suppress further review of a still-broken change.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the file in a copied project context instead of as a standalone file: create a tempdir, copy the repository subtree containing `source_paths` (or at minimum the target file’s package root plus sibling `.py` files and relevant tool config files), patch the sandboxed target there, and run pyright/ruff/bandit from that sandbox path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can run the supplied test command against the wrong codebase, so fix evaluation is not actually sandboxed. Evidence: it sets `cwd=tmpdir` but passes `test_cmd` unchanged. In this system the caller in `immune_agents.py` supplies `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. That path is not copied into `tmpdir`, so pytest either fails immediately or, depending on invocation/import resolution, executes tests from the real repository outside the sandbox. The code never rewrites paths or copies tests into the sandbox.
FOLLOW: This breaks the module’s key contract: “sandbox-test proposed fixes (SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL)” and “never modifies actual source.” A test run against the real repo can report `tests_passed=True` even though the patched file was never exercised, yielding false SAFE verdicts. Downstream, immune stage 4 may mark such fixes `verified=True`, causing closed-bug dedup and misleading the reviewer that a fix was programmatically validated when it was not.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when `test_cmd` is provided, copy the referenced test tree into the sandbox alongside the sandboxed source tree and rewrite repo-relative path arguments in `test_cmd` to their tempdir equivalents before execution; if that rewrite/copy cannot be done, set `tests_passed=None` and verdict `UNEVALUABLE` instead of running against live paths.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` judges harm using only the sum of net issue deltas: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; `if total_net > 0: HARMFUL`, `if total_net < 0: SAFE`. This allows regression cancellation. Example from the current fields: a fix that removes 5 ruff warnings but introduces 1 new bandit issue yields total_net = -4 and is marked SAFE.
FOLLOW: The verdict can silently approve fixes that introduce new security/type failures as long as they also remove more issues elsewhere. Because endocrine is used to set `verified=True` for SAFE/NEUTRAL fixes, a fix that newly breaks typing or security can still be treated as programmatically verified and close the finding in later rounds. That is a silently wrong result, which is HIGH in this PoC.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); only consider SAFE when no category regresses and at least one improves or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A mention like `brain.py` will match any source path containing that substring, and directory fragments in descriptions/fixes can collide across files. The function then falls back to the first source path if nothing exact is found.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation may patch and analyze the wrong file while still producing a normal verdict. That creates false SAFE/HARMFUL outcomes unrelated to the finding under review, wasting limited eval slots and potentially marking the wrong finding as verified. Since the evaluator is used mechanically by the immune pipeline, wrong-file targeting degrades both correctness and dedup closure.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — match target files by normalized exact path or exact basename equality only; if multiple source paths match the same basename, return `None` and mark the fix `UNEVALUABLE` instead of guessing.
VERIFIED: TRUE
